courses.title: Engineering Statics
courses.description: Cross Listed as: CE 2041 Two & three-dimensional equilibrium of particles & rigid bodies. Properties of areas including centroids, centers of gravity, & moments of inertia. Distributed loads. Analysis of 2D & 3D trusses, frames & machines. Static equilibrium & statically indeterminate systems. Principles of friction. Simplified load distributions on aircraft and rockets. Theory and application of principles on aircraft and rocket structures.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 1150 , MAT 115, or MAT 130; C or better in PHY 1510 or PHY 131; and C of better in PHY 1510L or PHY 131L.

courses.title: Engineering Statics
courses.description: Cross Listed as: ARO 2041 Two and three-dimensional equilibrium of particles and rigid bodies. Principles of friction. Properties of areas including centroids, centers of gravity, and moments of inertia. Distributed loads. Analysis of 2D and 3D trusses, frames and machines. Static equilibrium and statically indeterminate systems.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 1150 , MAT 115, or MAT 130; C or better in PHY 1510 or PHY 131; and C of better in PHY 1510L or PHY 131L.

courses.title: Process and Automation
courses.description: Cross Listed as: No Dual Listed as: No Comprehensive introduction to automation and control systems, focusing on fundamental electrical circuit principles and their applications. Basic circuit laws and components, progressing into DC circuit analysis. Alternating current (AC) principles, including the behavior of capacitors, resistors, and inductors in RC, RL, and RLC circuits. Key electronic devices such as diodes, transistors, and operational amplifiers (op-amps) are introduced, emphasizing their roles in electronic systems. Exploration of sensors, sampling, data acquisition, and PID controllers, preparing students to design and implement automation systems. Concepts will be reinforced through laboratory exercises that involve building real-world applications using the Arduino platform. Corequisite(s): CHE 2301L .
courses.prerequisites: MAT 215 or MAT 2140 ; CHE 201, CHE 2011 , IME 113L, or IME 1130L ; and C- or better in PHY 133 or PHY 1520 .

courses.title: Process and Automation Laboratory
courses.description: Comprehensive introduction to automation and control systems, focusing on fundamental electrical circuit principles and their applications. Basic circuit laws and components, progressing into DC circuit analysis. Alternating current (AC) principles, including the behavior of capacitors, resistors, and inductors in RC, RL, and RLC circuits. Key electronic devices such as diodes, transistors, and operational amplifiers (op-amps) are introduced, emphasizing their roles in electronic systems. Exploration of sensors, sampling, data acquisition, and PID controllers, preparing students to design and implement automation systems. Concepts will be reinforced through laboratory exercises that involve building real-world applications using the Arduino platform. Corequisite(s): CHE 2301
courses.prerequisites: MAT 215 or MAT 2140 ; CHE 201, CHE 2011 , IME 113L, or IME 1130L ; and C- or better in PHY 133 or PHY 1520 .

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: [GE 5A] Fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including atomic and molecular structure; nomenclature; stoichiometry; solution chemistry, including acid-base and redox chemistry; quantum theory; periodic properties; bonding theory; thermochemistry; gases; and intermolecular forces. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory experiments to illustrate and enhance lecture topics in CHM 1210 . Basic laboratory techniques and practices. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210 .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: Engineering, Society, and You
courses.description: The development of the individual in society from an engineering perspective. The study of the integration of society and technology. Development includes introduction to the fields of engineering and engineering technology, career planning, development of a community of learners, critical thinking, problem solving skills, and ethical and professional behavior. Analysis of typical problems involving technology in society and their solutions. Guest speakers. Exposure to campus resources and provides a framework for developing and implementing an academic plan culminating in the award of a four-year degree.

courses.title: Engineering, Society, and You Laboratory
courses.description: The development of the individual in society from an engineering perspective. The study of the integration of society and technology. Development includes introduction to the fields of engineering and engineering technology, career planning, development of a community of learners, critical thinking, problem solving skills, and ethical and professional behavior. Analysis of typical problems involving technology in society and their solutions. Guest speakers. Exposure to campus resources and provides a framework for developing and implementing an academic plan culminating in the award of a four-year degree.

courses.title: Project Design Principles and Applications
courses.description: [GE 5D] Selection and completion of scientific/technological synthesis application project under faculty supervision. Multidisciplinary team project. Projects that students solve in discipline of practice. Both formal written and oral reports.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Project Design Principles and Applications
courses.description: [GE 5D] Selection and completion of scientific/technological synthesis application project under faculty supervision. Multidisciplinary team project. Projects that students solve in discipline of practice. Both formal written and oral reports.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Project Design Principles and Applications
courses.description: [GE 5D] Selection and completion of scientific/technological synthesis application project under faculty supervision. Multidisciplinary team project. Projects that students solve in discipline of practice. Both formal written and oral reports.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Human Factors Engineering
courses.description: Study of Human Physiological, biomechanical, and psychological characteristics and how they influence engineering and design of equipment, machines, products, facilities, tools, and environments Corequisite(s): IE 2250L .

courses.title: Fundamentals of Human Factors Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Study of Human Physiological, biomechanical, and psychological characteristics and how they influence engineering and design of equipment, machines, products, facilities, tools, and environments, laboratory. Corequisite(s): IE 2250 .

courses.title: Operations Research I
courses.description: Application of optimization techniques to the problems encountered in industry & business. Problem formulation and software applications for solving linear & non-linear programming problems, including real, binary, integer, and combinations of variables. Solution methods, duality theory, and sensitivity analysis of linear programming. Analysis and report writing skills.

courses.title: Systems Engineering
courses.description: An introduction to Systems Engineering principles, covering both traditional (document-based) systems engineering and Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) approaches. Explore the system lifecycle, including requirements analysis, designing the system’s functional and logical architecture, designing the system’s physical architecture, and verification/validation. Through lectures, case studies, and hands-on lab assignments and projects, develop practical skills in both methodologies and MBSE soft-ware, and be prepared to apply these systems engineering frameworks and tools effectively in designing and developing complex systems. Corequisite(s): IE 3270L .

courses.title: Systems Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: An introduction to Systems Engineering principles, covering both traditional (document-based) systems engineering and Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) approaches. Explore the system lifecycle, including requirements analysis, designing the system’s functional and logical architecture, designing the system’s physical architecture, and verification/validation. Through lectures, case studies, and hands-on lab assignments and projects, develop practical skills in both methodologies and MBSE soft-ware, and be prepared to apply these systems engineering frameworks and tools effectively in designing and developing complex systems. Corequisite(s): IE 3270 .

courses.title: Project Management
courses.description: Introduction to project management, covering key aspects such as planning, scheduling, organizing, and controlling projects across various fields, including product development, construction, information systems, startups, and event management. Students will explore core topics such as strategy, priority setting, organizational structures, project management tools, and leadership. Emphasizes both high-level project management principles and a range of approaches‘“traditional and modern‘“along with practical techniques. As project management skills grow increasingly vital, students will gain proficiency in essential tools and concepts that offer a valuable competitive edge in today’s job market.

courses.title: Principles of Lean Implementation
courses.description: Lean characteristics, definitions, concepts, and trends; Use of various industrial engineering techniques in productivity improvement; Relationship between productivity and profit; Phases of a productivity improvement project; Lean Manufacturing, Just in Time, SMED, Cellular and Group Technology. Case studies. Plant visits and guest speakers.

courses.title: Operations Research II
courses.description: Applications of operations research techniques to the problems encountered in industry and business. Queuing theory, Markov analysis, and decision theory. Problem formulation and software applications. Quantitative analysis skills.
courses.prerequisites: IME 3140 or IME 3150 ; and IE 3160 or IE 4160.

courses.title: Capstone Course
courses.description: Analysis and design of systems for planning, scheduling and controlling production, inventory, energy, human resources and service operations. Use of computerized mathematical models. Projects and open ended case studies. Corequisite(s): IE 4620L .

courses.title: Capstone Course Laboratory
courses.description: Analysis and design of systems for planning, scheduling, and controlling production, inventory, energy, human resources, and service operations. Use of computerized mathematical models. Projects and open-ended case studies. Corequisite(s): IE 4620 .

courses.title: Discrete Systems Simulation
courses.description: Learn the principles of discrete-event simulation and apply simulation tools and techniques to analyze, improve, and design real-world systems in manufacturing and service industries, while developing practical problem-solving skills. Topics include systems theory, simulation model development, verification and validation, interpretation of simulation output, and technical report writing. Examine the use of generative AI tools to support learning and communication of simulation results, while critically evaluating AI-generated solutions for accuracy and relevance. Corequisite(s): IE 4290L .

courses.title: Discrete Systems Simulation Laboratory
courses.description: Learn the principles of discrete-event simulation and apply simulation tools and techniques to analyze, improve, and design real-world systems in manufacturing and service industries, while developing practical problem-solving skills. Topics include systems theory, simulation model development, verification and validation, interpretation of simulation output, and technical report writing. Examine the use of generative AI tools to support learning and communication of simulation results, while critically evaluating AI-generated solutions for accuracy and relevance. Corequisite(s): IE 4290 .

courses.title: Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering Computations Laboratory
courses.description: Fundamentals of digital computer methods, logic diagramming, programming in a high-level language. Computer solutions of elementary industrial and manufacturing engineering problems, laboratory.

courses.title: Industrial & Manufacturing Engineering Computations Laboratory II
courses.description: Intermediate knowledge of digital computer methods. Introduction to computational algorithms. Introduction to programming paradigms. Introduction to software management and portability. Introduction to interfaces to access various resources. Computer solutions of intermediate industrial and manufacturing engineering problems, laboratory.

courses.title: Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering Fundamentals Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to industrial and manufacturing engineering concepts, functions, lean manufacturing, teamwork, and project management. Includes study skills, time organization, engineering communications. Theory and application of work analysis as related to process design facilities, workplace layout, tools and equipment, and services. Analytical techniques of measurement of work content including stopwatch time study, standard data, predetermined time systems, computerized work measurement, and work sampling. Team project based on real industrial situations.

courses.title: Engineering Probability and Statistics
courses.description: Engineering applications of the concepts of probability, statistical distributions, statistical analysis, regression and correlation analysis, and probabilistic and statistical models. Estimation, hypothesis testing and confidence intervals. Corequisite(s): IME 3150L .

courses.title: Engineering Probability and Statistics Laboratory
courses.description: Engineering applications of the concepts of probability, statistical distributions, statistical analysis, regression and correlation analysis, and probabilistic and statistical models. Estima-tion, hypothesis testing and confidence intervals. Corequisite(s): IME 3150 .

courses.title: Facilities Planning, Layout and Design
courses.description: Concepts and methods used to design an effective facility layout and distribution systems. Topics include analysis of efficiency in layout designs as well as algorithms to design or improve them, concepts of flexible and cellular manufacturing, material flow analysis of distribution facilities, analysis and interpretation of data being used in logistics systems to inform facility design decisions, review of material handling systems and equipment, analysis and design of storage systems in various types of distribution centers, and evaluation of alternatives using analytical models.
courses.prerequisites: IME 326 or IME 3261 ; and MFE 126, MFE 1260, MFE 226, or MFE 2261.

courses.title: Production Planning and Control
courses.description: Principles of supply chain planning and control systems; Methods of forecasting, planning, scheduling, and controlling production, inventory and project activities; Quantitative models and computer systems.
courses.prerequisites: IME 2241L , IME 3140 or IME 3150 , and IE 3160 or IE 4160.

courses.title: Ethical Concepts in Technology and Applied Science
courses.description: [GE 3C or 5D] Explores ethics of engineers, scientists, and others involved with technology related to values, philosophy, ethical theory and practice, moral reasoning, morality in law and codes, professional standards, and societies-case studies. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.

courses.title: Fiscal Implications in Technical Decision Making
courses.description: [GE 4C or 5D] Economic theory of capital allocation decisions. Current and relevant views of managerial economics used to present a unified theory of capital allocation appropriate to private, public and governmental entities. Integrated application of economic and operations analysis to managerial problem-solving and decision-making processes. Study of inflation and tax consequences on economic decisions. Open to all majors.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Data Analysis: Application in Industrial and Systems Engineering
courses.description: Gain both theoretical understanding and hands-on experience using AI tools to enhance efficiency, productivity, and innovation in industrial and manufacturing systems. An in-depth exploration of artificial intelligence (AI) methodologies and their practical applications in the fields of industrial and manufacturing engineering. Learn foundational concepts in machine learning, deep learning, and data-driven decision-making, with a focus on solving real-world problems in manufacturing, supply chain optimization, process automation, and predictive maintenance. Key AI topics covered, such as data collection and preprocessing, regression techniques, supervised and unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning. Special emphasis will be placed on the integration of deep learning models, including neural networks and transformers, in industrial engineering applications.

courses.title: Statistical Quality Control
courses.description: Quality improvement concepts, Statistical Process Control (SPC), Control charts (variables & attributes), Process capability analysis, Acceptance sampling, Six Sigma, Gauge R&R. Corequisite(s): IME 4150L .

courses.title: Statistical Quality Control Laboratory
courses.description: History of quality and contributions of major figures, Quality management systems, six-sigma programs, and their implementation. Process control techniques, statistical analysis and other methods used to control costs, improve quality, and meet customer requirements. Six Sigma Green Belt Body of Knowledge. Corequisite(s): IME 4150 .

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: [GE 2] Functions, limits, continuity, derivatives of all functions including trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, inverse trigonometric, and implicit functions. Applications of derivatives, including max/min problems and L’Hopitals rule. Definite and Indefinite Integrals, The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, substitution rule and applications.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1050 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1052 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1055 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1070 ; AP PreCalculus >=3; or ALEKS Comp >=76.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: [GE 2] Integration techniques including integration by parts, integrals of trigonometric products, partial fractions, substitution and trigonometric substitution. Hyperbolic functions. Improper Integrals, sequences and series, polar coordinates, parametric equations and conic sections.
courses.prerequisites: AP Calc AB >=3, AP Calc BC >=3, or C or better in MAT 1140 or MAT 1140C.

courses.title: Calculus III
courses.description: Introduction to vectors, dot product, cross product, equations of lines and planes, calculus of vector valued functions, introduction to multivariable functions, differential calculus of multivariable functions, the chain rule, applications including extreme problems and Lagrange multipliers, integral calculus of multivariable functions, double and triple integrals, applications of double and triple integrals, line and surface integrals of vector fields, Green’s Theorem, the Divergence Theorem, Stokes’ Theorem.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1150 or MAT 1150C.

courses.title: Elementary Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
courses.description: Separable and linear ordinary differential equations; numerical and analytical solutions. Linear algebra: vectors in n-space, matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, diagonalization; applications to the study of systems of linear differential equations.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1150 or MAT 1150C.

courses.title: Engineering Graphics I
courses.description: Engineering graphics for product design, manufacturing and construction. Emphasis on graphic communication used for processing parts and layouts. Orthographic projection, pictorial views, section and auxiliary views, dimensioning for production-processing, and the four fundamental views of descriptive geometry. Use of instruments and CAD for engineering drawings. Corequisite(s): MFE 1260L .

courses.title: Engineering Graphics I Laboratory
courses.description: Engineering graphics for product design, manufacturing and construction. Emphasis on graphic communication used for processing parts and layouts. Orthographic projection, pictorial views, section and auxiliary views, dimensioning for production-processing, and the four fundamental views of descriptive geometry. Use of instruments and CAD for engineering drawings Corequisite(s): MFE 1260 .

courses.title: Manufacturing Systems and Processes
courses.description: Study of basic manufacturing processes with emphasis on terminology, technology, process principles and capabilities, material selection and comparative advantages and disadvantages. Processes discussed include material removal, joining, assembly, 3D printing and casting. Other topics include NC, measurement and gaging, and statistical methods. Corequisite(s): MFE 2010L .

courses.title: Manufacturing Systems and Processes Laboratory
courses.description: Study of basic manufacturing processes with emphasis on terminology, technology, process principles and capabilities, material selection and comparative advantages and disadvantages. Processes discussed include material removal, joining, assembly, 3D printing and casting. Other topics include NC, measurement and gaging, and statistical methods. Corequisite(s): MFE 2010 .

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Integrated Manufacturing and Automation
courses.description: Mechanization/automation/mechatronics. Problems and methods of mechanization. Material handling systems. Transfer lines. Elements of automation (sensors, actuators, drives, A2D and D2A converters). Automated inspection and identification techniques. Storage and Retrieval Systems. Control strategies: industrial control, discrete time/event-driven systems, feedback systems, Computer process control, and Programmable Logic Controllers. Robotic systems. NC machines and programming. Corequisite(s): MFE 4501L .
courses.prerequisites: MFE 2261 or MFE 1260 ; CHE 2301 ; and MFE 2010 , MFE 2211 , or MFE 2233 .

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Integrated Manufacturing and Automation Laboratory
courses.description: Mechanization/automation/mechatronics. Problems and methods of mechanization. Material handling systems. Transfer lines. Elements of automation (sensors, actuators, drives, A2D and D2A converters). Automated inspection and identification techniques. Storage and Retrieval Systems. Control strategies: industrial control, discrete time/event driven systems, feedback systems, Computer process control, and Programmable Logic Controllers. Robotic systems. NC machines and programming. Corequisite(s): MFE 4501 .

courses.title: Materials Science and Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals and applications of materials engineering. Atomic, molecular, and crystalline structures and properties of materials with their relevance to engineering. Topics will include: diffusion, defects, phase diagrams, heat treatment, mechanical behavior, and will cover the different materials classes, i.e., metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 1210 , CHM 1150 , CHM 121, or CHM 115; PHY 131 or PHY 1510 ; PHY 131L or PHY 1510L ; and MAT 116 or MAT 1150 .

courses.title: Introduction to Newtonian Mechanics
courses.description: [GE 5A] Introduction to mechanics, including Newton’s laws, vectors, statics, kinematics, conservation laws, rotational motion, Newtonian gravity, fluids, and simple harmonic motion. Corequisite(s): PHY 1510L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 114, MAT 1140 , MAT 1140C, MAT 115, MAT 116 or MAT 1150 ( MAT 1150 can be concurrent).

courses.title: Newtonian Mechanics Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Experiments in Newtonian mechanics. Corequisite(s): PHY 1510 .

courses.title: Introduction to Electromagnetism and Circuits
courses.description: Introduction to electricity and magnetism, including electrostatics, dc circuits, magnetostatics, electrodynamics, and Maxwell’s equations. Corequisite(s): PHY 1520L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 115 or MAT 1150 ; and C- or better in PHY 132, PHY 132B, PHY 1510B or PHY 1510 .

courses.title: Introductory Laboratory on Electromagnetism and Circuits
courses.description: Experiments in electricity and magnetism. Corequisite(s): PHY 1520 .

courses.title: Information Systems and Knowledge Management
courses.description: Introduction to the following concepts: Relational Databases Management (RDBM), data modeling, and computer-based knowledge systems used in modern manufacturing and service industries; Database design/development and management; Data retrieval using Structured Query Language (SQL) or other programming languages; Design of data pipelines to gather, retain, and disseminate useful system data; Use of AI for understanding and working with data.

courses.title: Reliability Engineering
courses.description: Study of reliability engineering concepts and methods for analyzing, evaluating, and improving system performance, with emphasis on failure modeling, failure data analysis and system reliability. Applications to industrial and business contexts highlight the impact of reliability on cost, sustainability, and organizational success.

courses.title: Applied Decision Theory
courses.description: Introduction to decision theory and its applications. Modern utility theory and its applications to decision making under risk. Applications of Bayesian Decision Theory. Emphasis on applications covering a wide range of both profit and nonprofit oriented institutions.

courses.title: Industrial Costs and Controls
courses.description: Engineering approach to cost recording, budgetary procedures and controls. Estimating production costs. Engineering problems. Current techniques in automating the cost recording and cost control functions.

courses.title: Special Topics for Lower Division Students
courses.description: Group study of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Industrial Applications of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics
courses.description: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence, its history and philosophy. Problem-solving through uninformed, informed, and nature-inspired search methods. Study of intelligent methods such as Expert Systems, Neural Networks, and Fuzzy Logic. Introduction to robotics and robot hardware and software. Study of obstacle avoidance and motion planning methods (roadmaps, potential fields, sampling-based). Applications and case studies in the service and manufacturing industries.

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Design of Experiments
courses.description: Introduction to design and analysis of experiments. Applications in product and process design and development; process correction and quality improvement. Taguchi’s loss-function approach to quality; signal-to-noise ratio analysis.

courses.title: Special Topics for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing and Metrology
courses.description: Application of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (ANSI Y14.5) to product design us-ing CAD. Application of the science of engineering measurements as used in inspection and quality control. Emphasis on the general use of scientific measuring devices and meas-urement assurance automated measuring systems. Corequisite(s): MFE 2430L .

courses.title: Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing and Metrology Laboratory
courses.description: Application of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (ANSI Y14.5) to product design using CAD. Application of the science of engineering measurements as used in inspection and quality control. Emphasis on the general use of scientific measuring devices and measurement assurance automated measuring systems. Corequisite(s): MFE 2430 .

courses.title: Manufacturing Metrology Laboratory
courses.description: The science of engineering measurement as used in inspection and quality control. Emphasis on the general use of scientific measuring devises and measurement assurance Automated measuring systems. Gage R&R studies.

courses.title: Net Shape Engineering
courses.description: Investigation of the various casting techniques characteristic of modern net shape production including foundry practice, the use of 3D printing technology. Green sand, sodium silicate, shell core, shell mold, investment, die casting and lost foam considered in relation to required molds, patterns, melting processes and materials. Computer applications include simulation software for mold system design. Corequisite(s): MFE 3341L .

courses.title: Net Shape Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Investigation of the various casting techniques characteristic of modern net shape production including foundry practice, the use of 3D printing technology and CNC. Green sand, sodium silicate, shell core, shell mold, investment, die casting and lost foam considered in relation to required molds, patterns, melting processes and materials. Computer applications include simulation software for mold system design. Corequisite(s): MFE 3341 .

courses.title: Robotics and Mechatronics in Manufacturing
courses.description: Principles of robotics and mechatronics in manufacturing systems. Topics include mechatronics concepts, sensors, actuators, robotic mechanisms, kinematics, robotic programming, mobile robots, and performance analysis of robotic systems. Corequisite(s): MFE 3610L .

courses.title: Robotics and Mechatronics in Manufacturing Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on experiments in robotics and mechatronics, focusing on sensors, actuators, robotic programming, mobile robot navigation, and mechatronic system integration. Laboratory sessions emphasize practical application of theoretical concepts covered in the lecture. Corequisite(s): MFE 3610 .

courses.title: Safety Engineering
courses.description: Principles of Safety Engineering applied to engineering industries. Control of noise, heat, electrical hazards, vibration, radiation, lighting, and air contaminants in the work place. Accident prevention. Material handling safety, machine guards and personal protection.

courses.title: Additive Manufacturing
courses.description: Introduction to basic principles and development of Additive Manufacturing (AM), description of AM methods (such as generalized process chain, vat photo-polymerization, powder bed fusion, extrusion-based processes, material jetting, binder jetting, sheet lamination, and directed energy deposition processes), direct write technologies, low cost systems, process selection guidelines, process-structure-property relationship, direct digital manufacturing, design for AM, rapid tooling, applications, business opportunities and future directions of the method.
courses.prerequisites: MFE 2010 , MFE 2211 , or MFE 2233 ; MFE 2430 or MFE 3221L ; and IE 4160 or IE 3160 .

courses.title: Smart Manufacturing
courses.description: Principles and applications of Smart Manufacturing and Industry 4.0 with integration of AI-driven tools such as generative AI for PLC programming, CNC Programming, and robotic control. Topics include SCADA, HMI, industrial IoT, digital twins, Smart Manufacturing Systems, Integration of robotics in manufacturing, smart sensors, and machine vision for quality control. Investigation of AI tools in design and optimization of automation systems. Hands-on labs using SmartCIM hardware, Siemens TIA Portal, LogixPro, CAM Assist, and GPT-powered simulations. Students analyze industrial data, generate AI-assisted solutions, and evaluate practical implications of intelligent automation. Corequisite(s): MFE 4250L .
courses.prerequisites: IE 3160 or IE 4160; MFE 4501 ; and MFE 3610 .

courses.title: Composites Manufacturing
courses.description: Current topics in plastics processing. Basics of composite properties; strength with respect to fiber loading-type and orientation. Processing methods for composite production; manual lay-up, vacuum, filament winding. Metal and ceramic matrix composites.

courses.title: Plastics Engineering
courses.description: Plastic materials and their processing. Review of the pertinent organic chemistry of polymer materials. Classification, properties, characteristics and applications of plastics; polyethylene, PVC, ABS, polyesters, phenolics and urethanes. Study of processes including injection molding, extrusion, thermoforming and blowmolding; applications, process parameters, quality, economics and tooling considerations. Corequisite(s): MFE 4380L .
